title: FAA Part 107 weather practice questions
description: Free FAA Part 107 weather practice questions: METAR and TAF codes, density altitude, wind shear, stability, icing, thunderstorms and 107.51 limits.

questions.question: Which two automated systems does the FAA Remote Pilot Study Guide name as playing a major role in gathering surface aviation weather observations?

options.A: PIREP and SIGMET
options.B: AWOS and ASOS
options.C: TAF and FB
options.D: AIRMET and FA

questions.explanation: The Study Guide says "Automated weather sources, such as the Automated Weather Observing Systems (AWOS), Automated Surface Observing Systems (ASOS), as well as other automated facilities, also play a major role in the gathering of surface observations."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: Automated weather sources, such as the Automated Weather Observing Systems (AWOS), Automated Surface Observing Systems (ASOS), as well as other automated facilities, also play a major role in the gathering of surface observations.

questions.question: Which of these is one of the conditions for which the Study Guide says convective SIGMETs are issued?

options.A: Severe thunderstorms with surface winds greater than 25 knots
options.B: Hail at the surface of 1/4 inch in diameter
options.C: Turbulence on the leeward side of a mountain
options.D: Tornadoes

questions.explanation: "Convective SIGMETs are issued for severe thunderstorms with surface winds greater than 50 knots, hail at the surface greater than or equal to ¾ inch in diameter, or tornadoes."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: Convective SIGMETs are issued for severe thunderstorms with surface winds greater than 50 knots, hail at the surface greater than or equal to ¾ inch in diameter, or tornadoes.

questions.question: According to the Study Guide, what does the modifier AUTO in a METAR denote?

options.A: The report came from an automated source
options.B: The report corrects an earlier report that contained an error
options.C: The report is a special report issued between routine reports
options.D: The wind direction is variable

questions.explanation: The Study Guide says "If the notation “AUTO” is listed in the METAR/SPECI, the report came from an automated source." A corrected report is marked COR instead.

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: If the notation “AUTO” is listed in the METAR/SPECI, the report came from an automated source.

questions.question: In a METAR wind group such as 14021KT, what do the first three digits indicate, according to the Study Guide?

options.A: The wind speed in knots
options.B: The peak gust recorded
options.C: The direction the true wind is blowing from, in tens of degrees
options.D: The direction the wind is blowing toward, in reference to magnetic north

questions.explanation: "The first three digits indicate the direction the true wind is blowing from in tens of degrees." The last two digits give the speed in knots.

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: The first three digits indicate the direction the true wind is blowing from in tens of degrees.

questions.question: How does a METAR show a temperature below 0 °C, according to the Study Guide?

options.A: The temperature is preceded by the letter M
options.B: The temperature is preceded by a minus sign
options.C: The temperature is given in degrees Fahrenheit instead
options.D: The temperature is preceded by the letter N

questions.explanation: The Study Guide says temperature and dew point are given in degrees Celsius and "Temperatures below 0 °C are preceded by the letter “M” to indicate minus."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: Temperatures below 0 °C are preceded by the letter “M” to indicate minus.

questions.question: In a TAF, what does the forecast visibility code P6SM mean, according to the Study Guide?

options.A: A 6 percent probability of precipitation
options.B: Forecast visibility greater than six miles
options.C: Visibility of 6 statute miles in precipitation
options.D: A forecast valid for the next 6 hours

questions.explanation: Forecast visibility is given in statute miles, and "If the forecast is greater than six miles, it is coded as “P6SM.”"

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: If the forecast is greater than six miles, it is coded as “P6SM.”

questions.question: According to the Study Guide, what is TEMPO used for in a TAF?

options.A: A rapid and significant change, usually within an hour
options.B: The probability of thunderstorms and precipitation in the coming hours
options.C: An amended forecast that replaces the routine TAF
options.D: Temporary fluctuations of weather, expected to last less than 1 hour

questions.explanation: "“TEMPO” is used for temporary fluctuations of weather, expected to last less than 1 hour." A rapid and significant change is coded FM, and probability is PROB30.

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: “FM” is used when a rapid and significant change, usually within an hour, is expected. “TEMPO” is used for temporary fluctuations of weather, expected to last less than 1 hour.

questions.question: Which set of conditions does the Study Guide list as resulting in a high density altitude?

options.A: Low elevations, high atmospheric pressure, low temperatures and low humidity
options.B: High elevations, high atmospheric pressure, low temperatures and low humidity
options.C: High elevations, low atmospheric pressures, high temperatures and high humidity
options.D: Low elevations, low atmospheric pressures, low temperatures and dry air

questions.explanation: "The conditions that result in a high density altitude are high elevations, low atmospheric pressures, high temperatures, high humidity, or some combination of these factors."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: The conditions that result in a high density altitude are high elevations, low atmospheric pressures, high temperatures, high humidity, or some combination of these factors.

questions.question: According to the Study Guide, how does aircraft performance change as air density decreases (higher density altitude)?

options.A: It increases
options.B: It does not change
options.C: It decreases
options.D: It increases only in humid air

questions.explanation: "As the density of the air increases (lower density altitude), aircraft performance increases. Conversely, as air density decreases (higher density altitude), aircraft performance decreases."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: Conversely, as air density decreases (higher density altitude), aircraft performance decreases.

questions.question: What does the Study Guide say happens as the water content of the air increases?

options.A: The air becomes less dense, increasing density altitude and decreasing performance
options.B: The air becomes denser, lowering density altitude and increasing performance
options.C: Air density stays the same because water vapor has no weight
options.D: The air becomes denser, lowering density altitude and decreasing performance

questions.explanation: "Water vapor is lighter than air; consequently, moist air is lighter than dry air. Therefore, as the water content of the air increases, the air becomes less dense, increasing density altitude and decreasing performance."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: Therefore, as the water content of the air increases, the air becomes less dense, increasing density altitude and decreasing performance.

questions.question: Which sequence does the Study Guide describe for an inadvertent microburst encounter by a small UA?

options.A: A tailwind, then downdrafts, then a headwind
options.B: Downdrafts, then a headwind, then a tailwind
options.C: A headwind, then a tailwind, then downdrafts
options.D: A performance-increasing headwind, then performance-decreasing downdrafts, then a rapidly increasing tailwind

questions.explanation: "During an inadvertent microburst encounter, the small UA may first experience a performance-increasing headwind, followed by performance-decreasing downdrafts, followed by a rapidly increasing tailwind."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: During an inadvertent microburst encounter, the small UA may first experience a performance-increasing headwind, followed by performance-decreasing downdrafts, followed by a rapidly increasing tailwind.

questions.question: How does the Study Guide describe the airflow down the leeward side of a mountain?

options.A: It flows smoothly and helps carry an aircraft over the peak
options.B: It follows the contour of the terrain and is increasingly turbulent
options.C: It becomes calm close to the terrain
options.D: It rises in steady upward currents

questions.explanation: "As the air flows down the leeward side of the mountain, the air follows the contour of the terrain and is increasingly turbulent. This tends to push an aircraft into the side of a mountain." The smooth upward flow is on the windward side.

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: As the air flows down the leeward side of the mountain, the air follows the contour of the terrain and is increasingly turbulent.

questions.topic: Ceiling, visibility and Part 107 weather limits
questions.question: What minimum distances from clouds does 14 CFR 107.51(d) set for a small unmanned aircraft?

options.A: 500 feet below the cloud and 2,000 feet horizontally from the cloud
options.B: 1,000 feet below the cloud and 2,000 feet horizontally from the cloud
options.C: 500 feet below the cloud and 1,000 feet horizontally from the cloud
options.D: 2,000 feet below the cloud and 500 feet horizontally from the cloud

questions.explanation: 107.51(d): the minimum distance from clouds "must be no less than: (1) 500 feet below the cloud; and (2) 2,000 feet horizontally from the cloud."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.51, Operating limitations for small unmanned aircraft (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The minimum distance of the small unmanned aircraft from clouds must be no less than: (1) 500 feet below the cloud; and (2) 2,000 feet horizontally from the cloud.

questions.question: According to the Study Guide, when does a temperature inversion exist?

options.A: When the temperature of the air decreases with altitude
options.B: When the temperature equals the dew point
options.C: When the temperature of the air rises with altitude
options.D: When atmospheric pressure rises with altitude

questions.explanation: "When the temperature of the air rises with altitude, a temperature inversion exists." Normally, "As air rises and expands in the atmosphere, the temperature decreases."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: When the temperature of the air rises with altitude, a temperature inversion exists.

questions.question: Which characteristics does the Study Guide's table list for stable air?

options.A: Cumuliform clouds and showery precipitation
options.B: Stratiform clouds and fog, continuous precipitation and smooth air
options.C: Rough air (turbulence) and good visibility
options.D: Cumuliform clouds and smooth air

questions.explanation: The Study Guide's table pairs unstable air with cumuliform clouds, showery precipitation and rough air, and stable air with "Stratiform clouds and fog", "Continuous precipitation" and "Smooth air".

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: Unstable Air Stable Air Cumuliform clouds Stratiform clouds and fog Showery precipitation Continuous precipitation Rough air (turbulence) Smooth air

questions.topic: Dew point, fog, frost and icing
questions.question: What two conditions does the Study Guide say are necessary for structural icing in flight?

options.A: Relative humidity above 50 percent and a temperature below 10 °C
options.B: Clear, dry air and a temperature below freezing
options.C: Flight above 12,000 feet and any cloud cover
options.D: Flying through visible water such as rain or cloud droplets, and a temperature of 0 °C or colder where the moisture strikes the aircraft

questions.explanation: "Two conditions are necessary for structural icing in flight": the aircraft "must be flying through visible water such as rain or cloud droplets" and the temperature where the moisture strikes it "must be 0° C or colder."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: Two conditions are necessary for structural icing in flight: 1. The aircraft must be flying through visible water such as rain or cloud droplets 2. The temperature at the point where the moisture strikes the aircraft must be 0° C or colder.

questions.topic: Dew point, fog, frost and icing
questions.question: What does the Study Guide say about frost on a small UA?

options.A: It poses no threat, like dew
options.B: It poses a definite flight safety hazard because it disrupts airflow over the wing and can drastically reduce lift
options.C: It increases lift but also increases drag
options.D: It matters only when the ambient temperature is above freezing

questions.explanation: "While dew poses no threat to a small UA, frost poses a definite flight safety hazard. Frost disrupts the flow of air over the wing and can drastically reduce the production of lift."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: While dew poses no threat to a small UA, frost poses a definite flight safety hazard. Frost disrupts the flow of air over the wing and can drastically reduce the production of lift.

questions.question: Through which three stages does the Study Guide say a thunderstorm cell progresses during its life cycle?

options.A: Cumulus, mature and dissipating
options.B: Cumulus, orographic and dissipating
options.C: Developing, squall line and mature
options.D: Mature, first gust and plow wind

questions.explanation: "A thunderstorm cell during its life cycle progresses through three stages-( 1) the cumulus, (2) the mature, and (3) the dissipating."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: A thunderstorm cell during its life cycle progresses through three stages-( 1) the cumulus, (2) the mature, and (3) the dissipating.

questions.question: During which stage does the Study Guide say all thunderstorm hazards reach their greatest intensity?

options.A: The cumulus stage
options.B: The dissipating stage
options.C: The mature stage
options.D: The orographic stage

questions.explanation: "All thunderstorm hazards reach their greatest intensity during the mature stage."

source.title: FAA-G-8082-22, Remote Pilot – Small Unmanned Aircraft Systems Study Guide (August 2016)

questions.evidence: All thunderstorm hazards reach their greatest intensity during the mature stage.

questions.topic: Ceiling, visibility and Part 107 weather limits
questions.question: What minimum flight visibility, as observed from the location of the control station, does 14 CFR 107.51(c) set?

options.A: 1 statute mile
options.B: 5 statute miles
options.C: 500 feet
options.D: 3 statute miles

questions.explanation: 107.51(c): "The minimum flight visibility, as observed from the location of the control station must be no less than 3 statute miles."

source.title: eCFR: 14 CFR 107.51, Operating limitations for small unmanned aircraft (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The minimum flight visibility, as observed from the location of the control station must be no less than 3 statute miles.
